title: A Shift in the Delivery Schedule
instructions: Listen carefully. Choose the option that best matches what is said or implied.

audio.description: Two colleagues adjust a work schedule after a supply delay.

transcript.text: The printed guides are stuck at the depot. We cannot run the session without them, can we?
We could use digital copies, but some people need paper. What if we begin with the demonstration?
That buys an hour, but delivery has no estimate. I do not want everyone waiting if the guides miss the afternoon session.
I will call the depot at noon. If there is no update, we can offer an online session today or meet tomorrow.
Keep today’s room booking for now. I will prepare a few copies in case the boxes arrive, and you can update the slides.
Agreed. Let’s explain the change is about materials, not the session itself.

questions.prompt: What problem has disrupted the plan?
options: The printed guides have not arrived.
questions.explanation: The printed guides are delayed because the boxes are stuck at a depot.

questions.prompt: Why is the digital version not a complete solution?
options: It cannot be shown in the room.
Some participants want to write on a paper copy.
The group has no internet access.
questions.explanation: One colleague says half the group wanted something they could write on.

questions.prompt: What will the second colleague do at noon?
options: Call the depot for an update
Email the supplier a new order
questions.explanation: They say, “I can call the depot at noon” to find out whether the materials will arrive.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of offering an online option?
options: To reduce the size of the group permanently
To replace the session with a written test
To avoid explaining the delivery problem
To avoid making anyone wait if the delivery is still delayed
questions.explanation: If there is no clear update, participants can join online or attend the next day rather than wait.
